examples.trans: He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Какой срок?
examples.trans: What's the deadline?

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to time'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: И сколько мне срок мотать здесь?
examples.trans: And how long do I have to serve my time here?

examples.text: Давайте отпразднуем освобождение узника.
examples.trans: Let's celebrate the prisoner's release.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'here'.

examples.text: И сколько мне срок мотать здесь?
examples.trans: And how long do I have to serve my time here?

examples.text: Подожди, я здесь уже.
examples.trans: Wait, I am already here.

examples.text: Да здесь я, здесь, дорогая.
examples.trans: Yes, I am here, right here, darling.

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'and', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А что, собственно, за условия?
examples.trans: And what,actually, is the condition?

examples.text: А завтра вы выходите ко мне на работу су-шефом.
examples.trans: Tomorrow you start working for me as my sous-chef.

examples.text: А заготовщиком можно и полгода пробыть.
examples.trans: And you can stay a prep cook for half a year.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('really') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or negation in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А это уж как ваш поручитель решит.
examples.trans: That is up to your guarantor to decide.

examples.text: Вы уж нас извините.
examples.trans: Please forgive us.

examples.text: Ты уж не сердись на меня.
examples.trans: Please don't be angry with me.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'how'.

examples.text: А это уж как ваш поручитель решит.
examples.trans: That is up to your guarantor to decide.

examples.text: Как новый шеф?
examples.trans: How is the new head chef?

examples.text: Погоняю вас напоследок, как в приличном ресторане.
examples.trans: I will run you ragged one last time, like in a proper restaurant.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'decide', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: А это уж как ваш поручитель решит.
examples.trans: That is up to your guarantor to decide.

examples.text: Давайте отпразднуем освобождение узника.
examples.trans: Let's celebrate the prisoner's release.

meanings.note: Russian perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to decide', forming an aspectual pair with 'решать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: А это уж как ваш поручитель решит.
examples.trans: That is up to your guarantor to decide.

examples.text: Суд решил.
examples.trans: The court has decided.

examples.text: Я решил.
examples.trans: I've decided.
